inheritanceRule: Every omitted field inherits the resolved parent class value.

profiles.name: Archer

evidence.section: Weapon and Armor Proficiency / Expert Archer
evidence.reason: The archetype gives up heavier armour and tower shields while dedicating its scaling weapon features to bows.
At high level the Archer can make one bow attack against every target in a 15-foot-radius burst.

profiles.playerSummary: A dedicated bow Fighter who performs ranged combat manoeuvres, shoots safely through a melee and eventually unleashes wide volleys.
profiles.tradeoff: Its defining training, defences and mastery are tied to bows, with less armour and less emphasis on close combat.

profiles.name: Eldritch Guardian

evidence.reason: A full-level familiar is central to the archetype and can share the Fighter's combat feats.
Operating a separate familiar with a changing set of shared combat feats adds substantial table management.

profiles.playerSummary: A Fighter who trains alongside a familiar, sharing combat feats so the pair can fight as a coordinated unit.
profiles.tradeoff: Early bonus feats and some martial class skills are exchanged for managing and protecting a second combatant.

profiles.name: Bolt Ace

evidence.reason: Crossbows replace firearms, gunsmithing and firearm proficiency throughout the archetype.

profiles.playerSummary: A Gunslinger engine rebuilt around crossbows, applying grit, deeds and weapon training without using firearms.
profiles.tradeoff: Its signature tricks are restricted to crossbows and it gives up the class's firearm identity entirely.

profiles.name: Gun Tank

evidence.reason: Heavy armour, shield use, critical and sneak-attack negation, bullet deflection and armour training define the package.

profiles.playerSummary: A heavily armoured Gunslinger who survives critical hits, deflects bullets and keeps moving effectively in armour.
profiles.tradeoff: Nimble and several bonus feats are replaced by a much more equipment-heavy defensive progression.

profiles.name: Forester

evidence.reason: The Forester explicitly has no animal companion and applies animal focus only to herself.
A scaling tactician progression repeatedly grants teamwork feats to nearby allies.
The archetype gains camouflage and eventually hides in favoured terrain while observed.
Removing the permanent animal companion eliminates an additional character sheet and combat entity.

profiles.playerSummary: A solitary Hunter who replaces an animal companion with favoured terrain, stealth mastery and shared teamwork tactics.
profiles.tradeoff: It loses the class's defining permanent companion and concentrates its teamwork and animal focus on the Hunter and nearby allies.

profiles.name: Primal Companion Hunter

evidence.reason: Temporary eidolon evolutions repeatedly reshape the animal companion, or the Hunter when the companion is dead.

profiles.playerSummary: A Hunter who spends primal energy to reshape an animal companion with a flexible selection of evolutions.
profiles.tradeoff: Precise teamwork tactics are reduced in exchange for another limited resource and a highly configurable companion transformation.

profiles.name: Monster Tactician

evidence.reason: A standard-action, minutes-per-level summon monster progression reaching summon monster IX becomes the defining combat feature.
Every summoned creature receives the Inquisitor's teamwork feats without needing to meet their prerequisites.

profiles.playerSummary: An Inquisitor who calls long-lasting extraplanar allies and turns them into a coordinated team through shared feats.
profiles.tradeoff: Judgments are surrendered, and managing summoned creatures becomes the centre of both tactics and table complexity.

profiles.name: Sanctified Slayer

evidence.reason: The archetype gains a scaling sneak attack progression alongside studied target and slayer talents.

profiles.playerSummary: An Inquisitor who marks one quarry, exploits openings with sneak attacks and selects talents from the Slayer and Rogue toolkits.
profiles.tradeoff: Judgments and their later improvements are replaced by a more martial, target-focused progression.

profiles.name: Forensic Physician

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype explicitly practises medicine, treats disease and analyses bodies, blood and medical evidence.

evidence.reason: Its named and mechanical identity is the professional examination and treatment of patients and physical evidence.

profiles.playerSummary: An Investigator who works as a medical and forensic specialist, reading bodies, blood and disease as evidence.
profiles.tradeoff: Trapfinding, trap sense and two investigator talents are exchanged for a deliberately narrow professional speciality.

profiles.name: Empiricist

evidence.reason: Intelligence replaces several different ability scores for important investigative, social and practical skills.

profiles.playerSummary: An Intelligence-centred Investigator who applies observation and reason to perception, motives, devices, information gathering and magic items.
profiles.tradeoff: Poison lore and resistance, swift alchemy and some trap talent are exchanged for unusually concentrated mental ability use.
